sources.quote: Pipeline mishaps unintentionally released nearly 9.7 billion cubic feet of gas into the atmosphere between 2019 and late 2023, according to a Reuters examination of incident report data maintained by the U.S. Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA).
sources.searcher_note: Pattern: Reuters totals gas lost in PHMSA incident reports; no Sea Robin, no 2025 data. Quote runs 38 words.

notes: Nothing found naming Sea Robin for any 2025 gas-loss report, the repeated 1,587,069 figure, or a 2025 record year. Sea Robin appears only in reference pages (Wikipedia, Global Energy Monitor wiki, Energy Transfer's own site). A 2022 Bloomberg story on an Energy Transfer gathering-line methane cloud in Louisiana surfaced (8.2 million cubic feet, July 22), but the BNN copy did not load and the search snippet did not tie it to Sea Robin; not recorded. PHMSA's Jan 2026 notice on OMB changes to gas incident report instructions (intentional vs unintentional releases, relief valves / emergency shutdowns count as intentional) bears on whether blowdowns belong in these reports, but phmsa.dot.gov returned 403, so no quote. No coverage of the unit ambiguity (cubic feet vs thousand cubic feet) for this operator found.
